label: Bible Study
prompt: Thy word have I _____ in mine heart, that I might not sin against thee.
verse: Thy word have I hid in mine heart, that I might not sin against thee.
note: From the longest psalm, all about God's word — memorization as a defense against sin.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: They shall come with weeping, and with supplications will I lead them: I will cause them to walk by the rivers of waters in a straight way, wherein they shall not _____: for I am a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my firstborn.
verse: They shall come with weeping, and with supplications will I lead them: I will cause them to walk by the rivers of waters in a straight way, wherein they shall not stumble: for I am a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my firstborn.
note: God leads the returning exiles by rivers of waters on a straight path where they shall not stumble.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And he was there in the wilderness forty days, tempted of Satan; and was with the wild _____; and the angels ministered unto him.
verse: And he was there in the wilderness forty days, tempted of Satan; and was with the wild beasts; and the angels ministered unto him.
note: Only Mark mentions that during the forty days of temptation Jesus was 'with the wild beasts.'

label: Deep Water
prompt: Nevertheless the foundation of God standeth sure, having this _____, The Lord knoweth them that are his. And, Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity.
verse: Nevertheless the foundation of God standeth sure, having this seal, The Lord knoweth them that are his. And, Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity.
note: God's foundation bears a two-sided seal: he knows his own, and his own turn from iniquity.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: Hast thou commanded the morning since thy days; and caused the _____ to know his place;
verse: Hast thou commanded the morning since thy days; and caused the dayspring to know his place;
note: 'Hast thou commanded the morning?' God asks Job. Zacharias later calls Jesus 'the dayspring from on high' (Luke 1:78).
